Long-Term Price Trend Analysis

Nike's stock has exhibited strong long-term momentum. The stock grew from a split-adjusted price of $4.47 in early 2000 to reach an all-time high (ATH) of $166.25 on November 05, 2021. The 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) illustrates the structural bull market Nike enjoyed post-2008 up until the recent post-pandemic adjustments.

Key Observation: The long-term trend highlights several multi-year compounding phases, particularly the 2010-2015 run and the aggressive 2020-2021 post-COVID stimulus rally.

Key Takeaways and Investment Implications

  • Robust Compounding: With a CAGR of 10.60%, Nike has proven to be an exceptional wealth compounder over a quarter-century horizon, significantly outpacing inflation.
  • Drawdown Tolerance: The risk profile requires an investor capable of withstanding drawdowns exceeding 40% during structural bear markets. Holding NKE is not without significant interim volatility.
  • Structural Resilience: Following every major market crisis (Dot-com bust, 2008 Financial Crisis, 2020 Pandemic crash), Nike's stock has historically recovered and pushed to new all-time highs, underscoring strong brand equity and pricing power.
  • Actionable Insight: For long-term allocators, periods of elevated volatility and deep drawdowns (approaching or exceeding 30%) have historically presented favorable accumulation points.
